- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates; increase forecast low by 5–10%.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward sentiment spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to peak values.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative, model often fails to reverse trend; adjust forecast to mean-revert toward 10–15 day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment volatility; dampen volatility by smoothing with 7-day rolling average.
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model often ignores it; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.0–0.5), model often overfits to recent highs; cap forecast at 1.5x recent 7-day high.
